summary.text: Josh Brecheen is the Republican incumbent for Oklahoma's 2nd Congressional District, which he has represented since 2023. A rancher and former excavation and trucking business owner, he served in the Oklahoma State Senate from 2010 to 2018. According to his official biography, he is focused on reducing federal debt and deficit spending.

paragraphs.text: Born in Pontotoc County, Oklahoma; graduated from Coalgate High School. His official biography describes him as a fourth-generation rancher from eastern Oklahoma.
Earned a dual degree in agriculture from Oklahoma State University and served as state president of the Oklahoma FFA Association from 1998 to 1999.
Ran a motivational speaking business, Brecheen Keynotes and Seminars, until 2010, and has raised performance horses for over 20 years, according to his official biography.
Worked for six years for U.S. Senator Tom Coburn as a field representative, and later owned and operated a small excavation and trucking business.
Elected to the Oklahoma State Senate in 2010, defeating Democratic incumbent Jay Paul Gumm; he served District 6 until 2018, when he did not file for re-election.

Won the August 23, 2022 Republican primary runoff for the open 2nd District seat over Avery Frix (52.2% to 47.8%), then the November general election with 72.4% of the vote, succeeding Markwayne Mullin.
Re-elected in 2024 with 74.2% over Democrat Brandon Wade and independent Ronnie Hopkins, and won the June 16, 2026 Republican primary with 79.2% over William Webb.

In the 119th Congress (2025-2026), serves on the House Budget Committee and the House Homeland Security Committee, where he is a member of the Emergency Management and Technology Subcommittee and chairman of the Oversight, Investigations, and Accountability Subcommittee.
Lives in eastern Oklahoma; his official biography describes him as a Christian, husband and father.
